day: # The Roman Lectionary for Mass: the weekdays (Monday to Saturday) of
# Advent, Christmas Time, Lent, Easter Time and Ordinary Time, as the
# Lectionary for Mass for use in the dioceses of the United States (second
# typical edition, 2002) gives them, from Felix Just's tables at
# Sundays, solemnities, feasts, Ash Wednesday, Holy Week and the Octave of
# Easter are in roman.csv.  Verses follow the New American Bible; a psalm's
# stanzas are joined where they run on, as in roman.csv.
# Ordinary Time has a two-year cycle for the first reading and psalm:
# cycle I in odd-numbered years, II in even (Year II for the weeks of 2026
# the church year from Advent 2025): `reading_cycle,abc; I II 2024`.  The
# Gospels, and every season but Ordinary Time, are the same each year;
# rows marked A, B or C are the Lectionary's other reading for that
# Sunday year (Advent 1 Monday, Lent 5 Monday, Easter 4 Monday, Ordinary
# The optional Masses of the third, fourth and fifth weeks of Lent (Lect. 236,
# 243 and 250, the Gospels of the Samaritan woman, the man born blind and
# Lazarus) "may be used on any day of this week, especially in Years B and
# C": each weekday of those weeks has them as a second set.
# Keys: Advent by its Sundays (the third week only before 17 December);
# 17-24 December, 29-31 December (not 30 December when it is the Holy
# Family) and 2-7 January by date until the Epiphany (none on a Sunday);
# the weekdays after the Epiphany by weekday when it is kept on a Sunday
# (as in the United States), by date (7-12 January) when it is not, until
# the Baptism; the days after Ash Wednesday and the weeks of Lent by their
# Sundays; the weeks of Easter 2-7 by days from Easter (the Thursday of the
# sixth week not where the Ascension is kept on it); Ordinary Time Weeks
# 1-9 from the Sunday of the Baptism (Week 1 begins the day after it, so on
# Tuesday when the Baptism is on Monday) until Ash Wednesday; and after
# Pentecost the weeks counted back from Christ the King, the 34th Sunday
# (next_start-7), from the Monday after Pentecost, as the Lectionary
# directs.  The Lent weekday Masses that may be used in any week (Lect.
# 236, 243, 250) and the Proper of Saints are not given; a saint's day
# with readings of its own in roman.csv is listed beside the weekday's.
# Kinds: ot (the First Reading, from either Testament, as roman.csv labels
# it), psalm (with canticles), gospel.  Citations as printed except: Ps
# 80:2ac+3b and the like keep their letters; Esther C:12 (the Greek
# addition) and Tobit 13 (Vulgate numbering) as printed; misprints in the
# table as read corrected to the Lectionary's verses: Year II Week 1 Tue 1
# Sam 1:9-20, Wed 1 Sam 3:19-20, Week 5 Sat Ps 106:19-20, Week 7 Thu Ps
# 16 Tue Mic 7:18-20, Week 22 Sat Ps 145:19-20, Week 24 Fri 1 Cor 15:12-20
# Week 30 Thu Eph 6:10-20, Week 32 Thu Phlm 7-20 (each read as "-22";
# Advent 2 Sat Matt 17:10-13 (a footnote mark run into the verse).
# For the General Roman Calendar: `readings,roman roman-weekday`.
